dedupe_keys.name: sivak lock and waterway traffic simulation

description: SIVAK (Simulatiepakket voor verkeersafwikkeling bij kunstwerken, a simulation package for traffic handling at waterway structures) is the simulation system Rijkswaterstaat has used since 1990 to analyse how ships are handled at locks, narrow waterways and other waterway infrastructure. It accounts for traffic composition and flow, operating strategy and traffic control, and typically reports waiting times, utilisation of waterways and waiting costs for different ship types per section. These calculations feed the Dutch Multi-Year Plan for Infrastructure, Spatial Planning and Transport (MIRT) to spot and prevent bottlenecks, and are used when designing new infrastructure. Because SIVAK II was written in the unsupported PROSIM language, Rijkswaterstaat selected Systems Navigator and Witteveen+Bos in 2019, with the maritime research institute MARIN as adviser, to rebuild it in a modern object-oriented simulation environment, later to run as a web solution. Coverage: Dutch locks and waterway objects. Access: internal to Rijkswaterstaat and its consultants; the public source is an announcement by the developer. Licence and cost: proprietary, available on request only. Caveats: no public documentation or code, and the status of the new version must be checked with Rijkswaterstaat. It supports lock capacity planning and waterway traffic flow studies. It complements the BIVAS network model, OpenTNSim and the EU fairway network graphs in the catalogue.
